rationale:
Single defect line is coherent: the fixing commit 47cd1687 ('MapCache: Prevent concurrent loads of the same key') is traced to issue 255 via traceability.verified_fix_issue_numbers=[255] and PR 398, and #255 is the supplied verified key. The pre-existing defect is visible in the buggy code itself: MapCache.get checked `!_map.containsKey(key) && ifAbsent != null` and awaited the loader with no record of in-flight loads, so two concurrent get calls for the same key both invoked ifAbsent. The production fix adds `_outstanding` and returns the existing FutureOr for a key already loading, which is exactly the behavior the trigger asserts (two overlapping `cache.get('test', ifAbsent: loader)` calls, expect count == 1). The minimized patch touches only lib/src/cache/map_cache.dart; the restructuring of get() into early returns is required to insert the in-flight check, and the changed tail `return null` is behaviorally identical to the old `return _map[key]` on that branch (key is known absent), so there is no unrelated refactor, feature extension, doc-only, config-only, or test-only content. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same commit and uses only the pre-existing public API get(key, ifAbsent:) with a plain delayed Future loader; it introduces no dependency on API added by the fix. Strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization runs shows all gates passed, including trigger.buggy_differential on 'test/cache/map_cache_test.dart::should not make multiple requests for the same key', trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups), trigger.fixed_clean, full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, full_suite.fixed_all_green, and build on both revisions. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #255 duplicates no registry entry.

One defect, one fix, one trigger, all aligned. The production change in lib/src/cache/map_cache.dart makes MapCache.get track in-flight loads in an _outstanding map so a second concurrent get for the same key awaits the existing FutureOr instead of invoking ifAbsent again. The trigger test 'should not make multiple requests for the same key' issues two overlapping cache.get calls with a delayed loader and asserts the loader ran once, which is exactly the missing-deduplication behavior the fix introduces; the pre-fix code path (!containsKey && ifAbsent != null -> await ifAbsent) has no guard, so the defect is pre-existing in the buggy revision rather than introduced by surrounding work. Traceability marks issue 255 as the verified fix issue via fix_commit_to_issue through PR 398, and the commit subject 'MapCache: Prevent concurrent loads of the same key' matches both patch and test intent. The minimized production patch is limited to the single get method plus the new private field and its doc comment; the restructuring into early returns is required by the new outstanding-load branch, and the trailing 'return null' is behaviorally identical to the removed 'return _map[key]' for an absent key in a Dart Map, so there is no unrelated refactor, feature extension, or config/doc-only content. The trigger comes from the unchanged upstream test portion of the same commit and uses only the pre-existing public Cache.get/ifAbsent surface, introducing no dependency on API added by the fix. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and google/quiver-dart#255 is the sole entry in allowed_root_cause_ids, so this root cause is not a duplicate. Strict evidence for both original and post-minimization runs reports all gates passed, including buggy differential reproduction of the single selector, deterministic fingerprints across 3 repetitions, fixed isolated/suite/reversed runs clean, and a green fixed full suite; no runtime claim is asserted beyond that supplied evidence.
